themes_detail.label: Damaged Tree Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Park Slope/Carroll Gardens experienced a spike of 14 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK—a 490% surge versus the 2.4-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.38)—suggesting concentrated storm damage, disease outbreak, or neglect across the district's tree canopy.
evidence: 14 damaged tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.4-complaint weekly baseline (490% increase, z-score 7.38)
Sustained trend in 90-day top-10 list (308 total complaints) signals ongoing neglect or recent trauma event
Community Board has repeatedly requested park upgrades and reconstruction, suggesting infrastructure backlog
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about what triggered the spike: weather event, disease, deferred maintenance?
Map complaint locations to identify if damage is concentrated in one park or district-wide
Investigate CB's years-long requests for park reconstruction—are tree issues a symptom of underfunding?

themes_detail.label: Sewer System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints surged to 16 THIS WEEK—a 237% spike from the 4.8-complaint weekly average (z-score: 4.06)—coinciding with the Gowanus neighborhood's major development investment, raising questions about aging infrastructure under strain.
evidence: 16 sewer complaints THIS WEEK vs. 4.8-complaint weekly baseline (237% increase, z-score 4.06)
Community Board has standing request to 'Inspect water main on specific street segment and repair or replace as needed'—suggests known infrastructure vulnerabilities
Timing correlates with $7.8B in neighborhood investment and $370M Gowanus refinancing (Brooklyn Eagle, March 18), potentially increasing demand on aging systems
reporting_angles: Interview DEP about sewer capacity in Gowanus/Park Slope during major development phase—are systems overwhelmed?
Cross-check which blocks are reporting failures; compare to DEP's water main inspection schedule
Investigate: Are developers required to upgrade sewer infrastructure as part of new projects, and is that happening?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Dumping Surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal dumping complaints jumped to 27 last week—a 238% increase from the 8.0-complaint weekly average (z-score: 5.6)—suggesting concentrated waste disposal problems tied to construction activity or inadequate sanitation enforcement.
evidence: 27 illegal dumping complaints last week vs. 8.0-complaint weekly baseline (238% increase, z-score 5.6)
1,003 DOB permit filings in last 90 days (630 alterations, 114 new buildings, 35 demolitions) suggest high construction activity generating waste
Complementary spike in dumpster complaints (6 last week vs. 1.5 baseline, 300% increase) points to overflowing or improperly managed waste containers
reporting_angles: Survey Park Slope/Carroll Gardens blocks for visible dumping; interview residents about problem locations
Cross-reference high dumping complaints with DOB permit locations—is construction waste being left behind?
Interview Sanitation Department about enforcement capacity during peak development season

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints surged to 14 last week—a 250% increase from the 4.0-complaint weekly average (z-score: 5.35)—potentially linked to the parallel spike in illegal dumping and suggesting coordinated pest management issues.
evidence: 14 rodent complaints last week vs. 4.0-complaint weekly baseline (250% increase, z-score 5.35)
Temporal correlation with 27 illegal dumping complaints (238% spike) and dumpster complaints (300% spike)—suggests waste accumulation attracting rats
Community Board has standing request for homeless services and park safety enhancements, potentially indicating conditions enabling rodent populations
reporting_angles: Interview Health Department about whether rodent spike is isolated to specific blocks or district-wide
Investigate link between illegal dumping hotspots and rodent complaint clusters—are they geographically aligned?
Report on Parks/Sanitation response times: how quickly are dumpster overflows and dumped waste being cleared?

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Street/sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 32 last week—a 184% increase from the 11.2-complaint weekly average (z-score: 4.77)—likely driven by construction activity and potential early signs of post-winter street work and traffic changes.
evidence: 32 street/sidewalk noise complaints last week vs. 11.2-complaint weekly baseline (184% increase, z-score 4.77)
1,003 DOB permits filed in last 90 days suggest ongoing construction generating noise
Peak-season street work and early spring activity typically increases this category; timing aligns with seasonal pattern acceleration
reporting_angles: Survey high-complaint blocks to identify primary noise sources: construction, traffic, or street vendors
Interview residents about construction noise during early morning/evening hours—are permits being violated?
Check DOB records for noise variance complaints filed by developers; are noise mitigation plans being enforced?
